metric: exposure fit -- linear-light mean luminance vs the photographs
fitTarget: the photographs' own mean linear-light relative luminance (Rec.709) over tools/luminance.py's population, minimising |render mean - photograph mean|. dE2000 is recorded on every row and was NOT used to choose any value.
population: tools/luminance.py hard-codes delta_e.py's poseVerified filter, so the fit target is the poseVerified population (serenity 2 of 11, kings-court 8 of 14). That is a fitting instrument, never a gate; the merge gate is read all-spot from tools/delta_e.py --all-spots. The all-spot luminance is recorded on every row as a diagnostic -- at serenity the two populations disagree by -0.010 (all-spot wants a brighter exposure, ~0.341), at kings-court by +0.016 the other way (all-spot wants ~0.535). The poseVerified population was used because a spot that fails pose verification photographs one subject and renders another, so its luminance difference is partly a framing error, and exposure fitted to it would compensate for that framing.
harnessMode: fixed-fov ("new zero"): ?apt=<id>&measure=1 with NO &fov=legacy, the camera that matches each photograph's own field of view, i.e. the one where render and photograph frame the same subject. Same mode plan 2 task 7 fitted in, so these rows are directly comparable to its table. The legacy 72-degree camera exists only to keep the gate number comparable with a historical threshold; fitting in it would have chased a known framing mismatch (measured: at 0.329 the legacy camera reads 0.0174 below the photographs where the fixed camera reads 0.0001 below).
bloom: DISABLED for every sweep row (bloom pass .enabled = false), per the phase's rule that exposure is fitted first with bloom off and bloom is then fitted with exposure fixed.
harness: Playwright headless Chromium with --use-angle=d3d11 --enable-gpu --ignore-gpu-blocklist (the default headless GPU is SwiftShader, which post.js's capable() rejects -- a run without these flags silently measures with no post chain at all). GPU reported by the runs: ANGLE (Intel, Intel(R) UHD Graphics 630, Direct3D11). photoSpot and spawn yaw were cross-checked against the raw JSON degrees on every page load (main.js converts once; a second conversion is ruled out by construction, not by inspection).
noise: materials.js randomises its procedural canvas textures on every page load, so two loads of identical code differ slightly. Measured here: linear mean luminance +-0.0004 (serenity) / +-0.0009 (kings-court) between loads, all-spot dE2000 +-0.01 to +-0.04. Rows captured in the same batch share one page load and one set of textures, so within-batch ordering is clean; across batches it is not.
windingDefect: This fit is against a render carrying a known, deliberately deferred defect: grid() in bake.js emits a fixed triangle order, so 8 of 12 wall faces are wound backwards and those walls present their far face, shaded from a point on the other side of the wall. Invisible today only because walls are flat-shaded MeshBasicMaterial. The human partner deferred the fix to a later plan with the accepted consequence that these constants will have to be re-fitted once the winding is fixed. Nothing here compensates for it and no measurement excludes walls.

chosen.why: closest tested value to the photographs' mean: pooled diff -0.00025 (-0.0004 refine 1, -0.0001 refine 2) against 0.328 -0.0011, 0.330 +0.0009, 0.331 +0.0014. dE2000 is flat at 16.19-16.24 (poseVerified) / 16.86-16.90 (all-spot) across the whole 0.327-0.332 bracket, so the two criteria did not disagree here and nothing was traded away.

batches.batch: refine 2 (independent page load, repeat of refine 1 plus 0.330)
batches.note: gives every candidate two independent measurements
first capture of the session, current shipped value, kept as a repeat point

batches.batch: same-load diagnostic, GATE MODE (legacy fov, bloom ON, shipped chain)
batches.note: not part of the fit -- run after the choice was made, to quantify what the exposure change does to the gate metric with everything else held constant
